title: The configured review skill reaches the phase reviewer, and a phase return that skips it is refused
description: Hotfix ordered by the owner before 3.9.0: since v3.2.0 the phase reviewer's brief never names the configured reviewSkill (audit-lookup.py phase_brief_parts never resolves it; drive-phase.py's dispatch_phase_review/dispatch_said/DISPATCH_PROMPT do not carry it), so no code review runs while /audit:status shows the skill.
desiredOutcome: On the drive route the phase reviewer's brief names the configured reviewSkill and the headless phase validation passes --skill; submit refuses a phase return whose phase resolved a review skill but whose return does not name it as invoked; with no skill resolved nothing changes; a live phase review with a skill still completes.

findings.issue: The resolved-skill check sits at submit, not at the one write every phase return passes through: `audit-task.py file-return <phaseId> --role reviewer --head <sha>` files a phase return with no `skillsInvoked` under a resolved skill, since `_phase_return_refusal` (audit-task.py) asks no skill question. That verb is still printed as the remedy by the sign-off refusal (audit-task.py:12289, 'file its return (audit-task.py file-return %s --role reviewer --head ...)') and documented at reference/verbs-in-full.md:1037. On the drive route it is NOT a bypass a user hits: the phase brief prints a `drive-phase.py submit` block (audit-lookup.py:2328), the drive files a phase review only through submit (drive-phase.py:12351), audit-reviewer.md allows the reviewer one submit and no other write, and no hook routes an agent to file-return. It is reached only by a hand-run, or by a model following the sign-off refusal's remedy text after a review was never submitted - exactly the case where the field would be missing.
findings.resolution: Hold the invariant at the sink: in audit-task.py `_phase_return_refusal` (audit-task.py already imports `_areas`) refuse a phase return whose `skillsInvoked` does not name `_areas.resolve_review_skill`'s answer, sharing one predicate with submit; keep submit's per-slice check, because the aggregate carries the union of the slices' lists. At minimum, make the sign-off refusal's remedy name `drive-phase.py submit <phaseId> --role reviewer --head ...` instead of `file-return`.

findings.issue: No case files a slice through `submit --slice n/N` under a resolved skill, so the claim that each slice's return is refused (brief text audit-lookup.py:666-669, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md submit paragraph, phase-signoff.md:32 'each slice's included') rests on statement order alone. Moving the check below the `--slice` branch, so that only the aggregated return is asked, keeps rq1-rq5 green: rq1-rq4 submit whole returns, and rq5 calls aggregate_slice_returns directly.
findings.resolution: Add a case that submits slice 1/2 with no `skillsInvoked` on a phase resolving a skill and asserts the refusal and that no slice return is held (slice_return_paths empty), and prove it red against the check moved after take_slice.

findings.issue: `_bare_skill` strips the qualifier on both sides, so a resolved plugin-qualified skill (`superpowers:code-review`) is met by a different plugin's same-named skill (`engineering:code-review`) - two distinct skills that both exist in a normal Claude Code install. The same leniency already exists in uninvoked_skills on the headless route, so this matches that route's vocabulary, but for a qualified resolved name it accepts a skill the plan did not name.
findings.resolution: Strip only the return side when the resolved name is bare; when it is qualified, accept the exact qualified name or its bare spelling and refuse a differently-qualified one - in one helper both submit and uninvoked_skills use, with a case for the differently-qualified spelling.

findings.issue: aggregate_slice_returns iterates `body.get(INVOKED_FIELD) or []` with no list check. With no skill resolved nothing refuses the field's type, so a slice writing `"skillsInvoked": "code-review"` aggregates to one entry per character (['c','o','d','e','-','r','v','i','w']) in the filed phase return.
findings.resolution: Read only list values (`v if isinstance(v, list) else []`), as skipped_review_skill already does, or refuse a non-list field on every phase return.

tasks.title: A phase return that skipped the resolved review skill is refused, and the phase brief says so
tasks.description:
Close the class, not only the instance: nothing checks that an Agent-dispatched phase reviewer actually invoked the review skill the phase resolved. Writer sessions are held by drive-phase.py uninvoked_skills() (it reads the runner's recorded skillsInvoked); the subagent route (the phase reviewer dispatched as an Agent, whose return is filed through `submit` / `brief --role phase` ... submit, with --head) has nothing.

Add the check:
1. The phase reviewer's return names the skill(s) it invoked (a field in the return object - reuse the name `skillsInvoked` the runner already records, so one vocabulary covers both routes). The brief section that audit-lookup.py writes for the phase reviewer (beside review_skill_lines(), added by the preceding task) tells the reviewer to invoke the skill and to list it in that field, and says why: a return without it is refused. Put ALL explanatory text in that brief section; plugins/audit/agents/audit-reviewer.md is at its byte ceiling (measure-context / its size lint) - do not grow it.
2. `submit` for a phase return refuses when the phase resolved a review skill and the return does not name it as invoked. The refusal states the reason and the remedy (invoke the skill, then resubmit with it listed) in the drive's own refusal style. When no skill resolved, nothing changes: a return without the field is accepted exactly as today (prove it with a case).
3. Red-first BOTH directions, with the failing line quoted: (a) a phase that resolved a skill + a return without it -> refused (the case is red against the code without the check); (b) the allow side: no skill resolved + no field -> accepted, and a resolved skill + the field naming it -> accepted (the case is red against a check that over-fires, e.g. one that refuses whenever the field is absent).
4. If this turns out to need an architecture change (e.g. the phase return has no seam where the resolved skill is known at submit time), STOP and say so in the return instead of building it.

Read writing-python, no-silent-pass, before-you-claim. No register ids in comments.
